blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Factorize the following: \(a^{2}+4b^{2}\)
blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh factorization ka sawal hai: humein \(a^{2}+4b^{2}\) ko do factors (aise hisse jo aapas mein zarb ho kar poora expression banayein) ke product ki shakal mein likhna hai. Yeh do squares ka sum (jor) hai. Pichli classes mein aap ne parha tha ke sum of squares ke factors nahi bante; woh baat real numbers ke liye sahi thi. Ab hamare paas \(i\) hai, aur \(i^{2}=-1\) plus sign ko minus mein badal deta hai. Plan: pehle dono terms ko square ki shakal mein likhenge, phir \(i\) ki madad se sum ko difference of squares banayenge, aur aakhir mein \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagayenge.
steps:
Step 1: Dono terms ko square ki shakal mein likhein
\[4b^{2}=(2b)^{2}\]
\[a^{2}+4b^{2}=a^{2}+(2b)^{2}\]
Kyun: Difference of squares ka formula tabhi lagta hai jab har term kisi cheez ka square ho. \(a^{2}\) to pehle se square hai. \(4b^{2}\) ko ghaur se dekhiye: \(2b\) ko \(2b\) se zarb dein to \(4b^{2}\) banta hai, yaani yeh \(2b\) ka square hai.

Step 2: i ki madad se plus ko minus banayein
\[(2bi)^{2}=4b^{2}i^{2}=-4b^{2}\]
\[a^{2}+(2b)^{2}=a^{2}-(2bi)^{2}\]
Kyun: Yeh is sawal ki asal chaabi hai. \(i^{2}=-1\) hai, is liye \((2bi)^{2}\) ki value \(-4b^{2}\) hai. Ab \(+4b^{2}\) likhna aur \(-(2bi)^{2}\) likhna bilkul ek hi baat hai, kyun ke minus ka minus plus hota hai. Is tarah sum ab difference ban gaya.
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students \((2bi)^{2}\) ko \(4b^{2}i\) likh dete hain. Square poore bracket ka hota hai: 2 ka bhi, \(b\) ka bhi aur \(i\) ka bhi, yaani \(4b^{2}i^{2}\).

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[a^{2}-(2bi)^{2}\]
\[=(a+2bi)(a-2bi)\]
Kyun: Ab expression bilkul \(A^{2}-B^{2}\) ki shakal mein hai, jahan \(A=a\) aur \(B=2bi\). Formula \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) seedha lagaya: ek factor mein plus, doosre mein minus. Ghaur karein ke dono factors ek doosre ke conjugate (jora, jis mein sirf \(i\) wale hisse ka sign ulta ho) hain.

Tasdeeq: factors ko wapas multiply karein
\[(a+2bi)(a-2bi)\]
\[=a^{2}-4b^{2}i^{2}\]
\[=a^{2}+4b^{2}\]
Kyun: Factorization check karne ka sab se pakka tareeqa yeh hai ke factors ko wapas zarb dein. Beech wali terms \(+2abi\) aur \(-2abi\) cancel ho jaati hain, aur \(-4b^{2}i^{2}\) ban jaata hai \(+4b^{2}\). Wahi expression wapas mil gaya, is liye factors durust hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(a^{2}+4b^{2}=(a+2bi)(a-2bi)\). Matlab: jo sum real numbers mein nahi toot-ta tha, woh complex numbers mein do conjugate factors mein toot gaya.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Factorize the following: \(9a^{2}+16b^{2}\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal bilkul (i) ki tarah hai, sirf numbers bare hain. Humein \(9a^{2}+16b^{2}\) ke factors chahiye. Sab se pehle pehchaniye ke dono terms perfect squares hain: \(9a^{2}=(3a)^{2}\) aur \(16b^{2}=(4b)^{2}\). Phir wahi chaal chalni hai: \(i^{2}=-1\) ki madad se \(+(4b)^{2}\) ko \(-(4bi)^{2}\) likhenge taa ke difference of squares ban jaaye, aur formula \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) laga denge.
steps:
Step 1: Dono terms ko square ki shakal mein likhein
\[9a^{2}=(3a)^{2}\]
\[16b^{2}=(4b)^{2}\]
Kyun: \(3^{2}=9\) aur \(4^{2}=16\) hain, is liye dono terms perfect squares hain. Coefficient ka square root aur variable ka square root dono saath lene hain: \(\sqrt{9a^{2}}=3a\).

Step 2: Plus ko minus banayein
\[(4bi)^{2}=16b^{2}i^{2}=-16b^{2}\]
\[9a^{2}+16b^{2}=(3a)^{2}-(4bi)^{2}\]
Kyun: \(i^{2}=-1\) ki wajah se \((4bi)^{2}\) negative hai, yaani \(-16b^{2}\). Is liye \(-(4bi)^{2}\) asal mein \(+16b^{2}\) hi hai. Humne value nahi badli, sirf likhne ka tareeqa badla hai.
Dhyan dein: \(i\) hamesha us term ke saath lagta hai jo plus wala square hai aur jise hum minus banana chahte hain; yahan woh \(4b\) hai.

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[(3a)^{2}-(4bi)^{2}\]
\[=(3a+4bi)(3a-4bi)\]
Kyun: Ab \(A=3a\) aur \(B=4bi\) le kar formula \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya. Dono factors phir se conjugates hain: real hissa \(3a\) same, imaginary hissa \(4b\) ka sign ulta.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(3a+4bi)(3a-4bi)\]
\[=9a^{2}-16b^{2}i^{2}\]
\[=9a^{2}+16b^{2}\]
Kyun: Conjugates ko zarb dene par beech ki terms khatam ho jaati hain aur \(-16b^{2}i^{2}=+16b^{2}\) banta hai. Product wahi expression hai jo diya gaya tha, to jawab pakka hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(9a^{2}+16b^{2}=(3a+4bi)(3a-4bi)\). Do conjugate factors, jaisa sum of squares mein hamesha hota hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Factorize the following: \(3x^{2}+3y^{2}\)
blocks.explanation: Is sawal mein ek chhota sa farq hai: dono terms mein 3 common hai. Ek achhe student ki aadat honi chahiye ke factorization mein sab se pehle common factor dekhe. 3 bahar nikaalne ke baad andar \(x^{2}+y^{2}\) bachta hai, jo squares ka sum hai. Usko hum \(i\) ki madad se difference of squares bana kar factorize karenge. Aakhir mein 3 ko jawab ke aage zaroor rakhna hai.
steps:
Step 1: Common factor 3 bahar nikaalein
\[3x^{2}+3y^{2}=3(x^{2}+y^{2})\]
Kyun: Hamesha pehle common factor bahar nikaalein. Is se bracket chhota aur saaf ho jaata hai, aur aage ka kaam aasaan ho jaata hai. \(3x^{2}\) ko perfect square banane ki koshish karte to \(\sqrt{3}\) aa jaata, jo bila wajah mushkil hai.

Step 2: Sum ko difference banayein
\[(iy)^{2}=i^{2}y^{2}=-y^{2}\]
\[x^{2}+y^{2}=x^{2}-(iy)^{2}\]
Kyun: \(i^{2}=-1\) ki wajah se \((iy)^{2}=-y^{2}\). Is liye \(+y^{2}\) ki jagah \(-(iy)^{2}\) likhna jaaiz hai; value wahi rehti hai, sirf shakal difference of squares wali ho jaati hai.

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[3\left(x^{2}-(iy)^{2}\right)\]
\[=3(x+iy)(x-iy)\]
Kyun: Bracket ke andar \(A=x\) aur \(B=iy\) hain, to \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) seedha laga. Dilchasp baat: \(x+iy\) wahi complex number ki standard shakal hai, aur \(x-iy\) uska conjugate.
Dhyan dein: Step 1 wala 3 aage hi rehta hai. Usko bhool jaana is sawal ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[3(x+iy)(x-iy)\]
\[=3(x^{2}-i^{2}y^{2})\]
\[=3x^{2}+3y^{2}\]
Kyun: Pehle conjugates ko zarb diya, \(-i^{2}y^{2}=+y^{2}\) bana, phir 3 se zarb diya. Wahi expression wapas mil gaya.
blocks.final_answer: \(3x^{2}+3y^{2}=3(x+iy)(x-iy)\). Yaani 3 aur ek complex number aur uske conjugate ka product.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Factorize the following: \(144x^{2}+225y^{2}\)
blocks.explanation: Yahan numbers bare hain, is liye ghabraiye nahi; pehle dekhiye ke 144 aur 225 mein kya common hai. \(144=9\times16\) aur \(225=9\times25\), yaani 9 dono mein common hai. 9 bahar nikaalne se andar \(16x^{2}+25y^{2}\) bachta hai, jis mein dono terms perfect squares hain. Phir wahi tareeqa: \(i\) se plus ko minus banayein aur difference of squares lagayein.
steps:
Step 1: Common factor 9 bahar nikaalein
\[144x^{2}+225y^{2}\]
\[=9(16x^{2}+25y^{2})\]
Kyun: 9, 144 aur 225 ka sab se bara common factor (HCF) hai. Sab se bara common factor nikaalne se bracket sab se chhota aur saaf ban jaata hai. (Waise \(144=12^{2}\) aur \(225=15^{2}\) bhi hain; us raste se bhi same jawab aata, bas 9 baad mein nikalta.)

Step 2: Bracket ko difference of squares banayein
\[16x^{2}=(4x)^{2}\]
\[25y^{2}=(5y)^{2}=-(5yi)^{2}\]
\[16x^{2}+25y^{2}=(4x)^{2}-(5yi)^{2}\]
Kyun: \((5yi)^{2}=25y^{2}i^{2}=-25y^{2}\) hai, is liye \(+25y^{2}=-(5yi)^{2}\). Ab bracket ke andar ek square minus doosra square hai.

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[9\left((4x)^{2}-(5yi)^{2}\right)\]
\[=9(4x+5yi)(4x-5yi)\]
Kyun: \(A=4x\) aur \(B=5yi\) le kar \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya. 9 bahar wese hi likha rehta hai.
Dhyan dein: Answer key yahi factors \(9(4x+i5y)(4x-i5y)\) likhti hai. \(5yi\) aur \(i5y\) ek hi cheez hain, kyun ke zarb mein tarteeb (order) se farq nahi padta.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[9(16x^{2}-25y^{2}i^{2})\]
\[=9(16x^{2}+25y^{2})\]
\[=144x^{2}+225y^{2}\]
Kyun: Conjugates ka product \(16x^{2}+25y^{2}\) aaya, aur 9 se zarb dene par asal expression wapas mil gaya. Is liye jawab durust hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(144x^{2}+225y^{2}=9(4x+5yi)(4x-5yi)\). Pehle HCF, phir conjugate factors: yahi tarteeb yaad rakhiye.

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Factorize the following: \(z^{2}-2iz-1\)
blocks.explanation: Ab sawal ki qism badal gayi: yeh \(z\) mein quadratic (degree 2) expression hai, aur iske coefficients mein \(i\) bhi hai. Aise expression ko hum perfect square \((z-k)^{2}=z^{2}-2kz+k^{2}\) se milate hain. Beech wali term \(-2iz\) ko \(-2kz\) se milaiye: saaf pata chalta hai ke \(k=i\) hona chahiye. Ab dekhna yeh hai ke constant term \(-1\) bilkul \(k^{2}\) hai ya kuch baqi bachta hai. Plan: completing the square karein aur check karein.
steps:
Step 1: z ke coefficient ka aadha lein aur uska square karein
\[\dfrac{-2i}{2}=-i\]
\[(-i)^{2}=i^{2}=-1\]
Kyun: Completing the square mein hamesha (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) chahiye hota hai, kyun ke \((z+p)^{2}=z^{2}+2pz+p^{2}\) mein beech wali term ka aadha \(p\) hai. Yahan woh square \(-1\) aata hai.
Dhyan dein: \((-i)^{2}\) ko \(+1\) mat likhiye. \((-i)^{2}=(-1)^{2}\,i^{2}=1\times(-1)=-1\).

Step 2: Dekhein ke constant pehle se hi yahi square hai
\[z^{2}-2iz-1\]
\[=z^{2}-2iz+(-i)^{2}\]
\[=(z-i)^{2}\]
Kyun: Constant term \(-1\) bilkul \((-i)^{2}\) ke barabar hai. Is liye poora expression khud hi ek perfect square hai aur kuch baqi nahi bachta; difference of squares ki zaroorat hi nahi padi.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(z-i)(z-i)\]
\[=z^{2}-iz-iz+i^{2}\]
\[=z^{2}-2iz-1\]
Kyun: Har term ko har term se zarb diya: \(-iz-iz=-2iz\) aur \(i^{2}=-1\). Wahi expression mil gaya. Dono linear factors barabar hain, yaani root \(z=i\) do dafa aata hai (isko repeated root kehte hain).
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{2}-2iz-1=(z-i)(z-i)=(z-i)^{2}\). Yaani yeh ek perfect square hai aur iska root \(z=i\) do dafa aata hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Factorize the following: \(z^{2}+6z+13\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh \(z\) mein aam quadratic hai, lekin real numbers mein iske factors nahi bante: discriminant \(b^{2}-4ac=36-52\) negative hai. Jab discriminant negative ho to samajh jaaiye ke factors complex honge. Tareeqa: pehle completing the square karenge, phir jo positive number bache usko \(-(\ldots i)^{2}\) likh kar difference of squares bana denge.
steps:
Step 1: Completing the square
\[\left(\dfrac{6}{2}\right)^{2}=9\]
\[z^{2}+6z+13=(z^{2}+6z+9)+4\]
\[=(z+3)^{2}+4\]
Kyun: 6 ka aadha 3 hai aur \(3^{2}=9\). Is liye 13 ko \(9+4\) mein toda, taa ke \(z^{2}+6z+9\) poora square \((z+3)^{2}\) ban jaaye. Humne kuch joda ya ghataya nahi; 13 ko sirf do hisson mein likha hai.

Step 2: +4 ko minus square likhein
\[(2i)^{2}=4i^{2}=-4\]
\[(z+3)^{2}+4=(z+3)^{2}-(2i)^{2}\]
Kyun: \((2i)^{2}=-4\) hai, is liye 4 jorna aur \((2i)^{2}\) ghataana bilkul ek hi baat hai. Ab ek square minus doosra square ban gaya.

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[(z+3)^{2}-(2i)^{2}\]
\[=(z+3+2i)(z+3-2i)\]
Kyun: Yahan \(A=z+3\) poora ek block hai aur \(B=2i\). Formula \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya.
Dhyan dein: \(z+3\) ko ek hi cheez samjhiye; bracket ko tor kar sirf \(z\) ya sirf 3 ke saath \(i\) mat lagaiye.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(z+3)^{2}-(2i)^{2}\]
\[=z^{2}+6z+9+4\]
\[=z^{2}+6z+13\]
Kyun: \((z+3)^{2}\) ko khola aur \(-(2i)^{2}=+4\) joda. Asal expression wapas mil gaya, is liye factors sahih hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{2}+6z+13=(z+3+2i)(z+3-2i)\). Iske roots \(-3-2i\) aur \(-3+2i\) hain, jo aapas mein conjugate hain.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vii) Factorize the following: \(z^{2}+4z+5\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh bilkul (vi) jaisa sawal hai, is liye wahi raasta istemal karenge. Discriminant \(16-20\) negative hai, to factors complex honge. Completing the square karenge, jo \(+1\) bache usko \(-i^{2}\) likhenge, phir difference of squares lagayenge. Aap khud bhi pehle try kijiye, phir neeche se milaiye.
steps:
Step 1: Completing the square
\[\left(\dfrac{4}{2}\right)^{2}=4\]
\[z^{2}+4z+5=(z^{2}+4z+4)+1\]
\[=(z+2)^{2}+1\]
Kyun: 4 ka aadha 2 aur \(2^{2}=4\). Is liye 5 ko \(4+1\) mein toda; \(z^{2}+4z+4\) poora square \((z+2)^{2}\) hai.

Step 2: +1 ko minus square likhein
\[i^{2}=-1\]
\[(z+2)^{2}+1=(z+2)^{2}-i^{2}\]
Kyun: \(-i^{2}=-(-1)=+1\) hota hai, is liye \(+1\) ki jagah \(-i^{2}\) likhna jaaiz hai. Yahan \(B=i\) khud hi kaafi hai, kyun ke 1 ka square root 1 hai.

Step 3: Difference of squares lagayein
\[(z+2)^{2}-i^{2}\]
\[=(z+2+i)(z+2-i)\]
Kyun: \(A=z+2\) aur \(B=i\) le kar \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya. Dobara do conjugate factors mile.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(z+2)^{2}-i^{2}\]
\[=z^{2}+4z+4+1\]
\[=z^{2}+4z+5\]
Kyun: Square khola aur \(-i^{2}=+1\) joda. Product wahi expression hai, is liye jawab durust hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{2}+4z+5=(z+2+i)(z+2-i)\). Roots \(-2\pm i\) hain, ek conjugate pair.

blocks.prompt: 1 (viii) [printed as (vii)] Factorize the following: \(2z^{2}-22z+65\)
blocks.explanation: Is quadratic mein ek nayi baat hai: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 nahi, balke 2 hai. Completing the square ka formula (aadhe ka square) tabhi seedha lagta hai jab \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 ho. Is liye pehle 2 bahar nikaalenge, phir bracket ke andar completing the square karenge, aur jo positive fraction bache usko \(i\) se minus square banayenge. Aakhir tak 2 ko aage sambhaal kar rakhna hai; yahi is sawal ka imtihaan hai.
steps:
Step 1: Leading coefficient 2 bahar nikaalein
\[2z^{2}-22z+65\]
\[=2\left(z^{2}-11z+\dfrac{65}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: Leading coefficient (sab se bari power wali term ka coefficient) 2 hai. Har term ko 2 se divide kar ke 2 bahar likha, taa ke andar \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 ho jaaye. 65 taaq (odd) hai, is liye \(\frac{65}{2}\) fraction aata hai; is se ghabraiye nahi.

Step 2: Aadhe ka square nikaalein
\[\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{121}{4}\]
\[\dfrac{65}{2}=\dfrac{130}{4}=\dfrac{121}{4}+\dfrac{9}{4}\]
Kyun: \(-11\) ka aadha \(-\frac{11}{2}\) hai aur uska square \(\frac{121}{4}\). Constant \(\frac{65}{2}\) ko bhi chautha hisson mein likha (\(\frac{130}{4}\)) taa ke dekh saken ke square poora karne ke baad kitna bachta hai: \(\frac{9}{4}\).

Step 3: Andar completing the square
\[z^{2}-11z+\dfrac{65}{2}\]
\[=\left(z-\dfrac{11}{2}\right)^{2}+\dfrac{9}{4}\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}-11z+\frac{121}{4}\) poora square \(\left(z-\frac{11}{2}\right)^{2}\) hai, aur baqi \(\frac{9}{4}\) alag likha.

Step 4: Baqi hisse ko minus square likhein
\[\left(\dfrac{3i}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{9i^{2}}{4}=-\dfrac{9}{4}\]
\[\left(z-\dfrac{11}{2}\right)^{2}-\left(\dfrac{3i}{2}\right)^{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{9}{4}\) ka square root \(\frac{3}{2}\) hai, aur \(i\) lagane se square negative ho jaata hai. Yaani \(+\frac{9}{4}=-\left(\frac{3i}{2}\right)^{2}\); ab difference of squares ban gaya.

Step 5: Factorize karein aur 2 wapas lagayein
\[\left(z-\dfrac{11}{2}+\dfrac{3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\dfrac{11}{2}-\dfrac{3i}{2}\right)\]
\[=\left(z-\dfrac{11-3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\dfrac{11+3i}{2}\right)\]
\[2z^{2}-22z+65\]
\[=2\left(z-\dfrac{11-3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\dfrac{11+3i}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: \(A=z-\frac{11}{2}\), \(B=\frac{3i}{2}\) le kar \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya, phir har factor ko \((z-\text{root})\) ki shakal mein likha.
Dhyan dein: Step 1 mein jo 2 bahar nikala tha woh aage lazmi rakhna hai, warna product diye gaye polynomial ka sirf aadha hoga. (Answer key yahi ghalti karti hai; neeche dekhiye.)

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[\left(z-\dfrac{11}{2}\right)^{2}+\dfrac{9}{4}\]
\[=z^{2}-11z+\dfrac{130}{4}\]
\[2\left(z^{2}-11z+\dfrac{65}{2}\right)=2z^{2}-22z+65\]
Kyun: Factors ka product bracket wala quadratic deta hai, aur usko 2 se zarb dene par wahi polynomial wapas mil jaata hai. Is se yeh bhi saaf hai ke 2 ke baghair jawab adhoora hota.
blocks.final_answer: \(2z^{2}-22z+65=2\left(z-\frac{11-3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\frac{11+3i}{2}\right)\). Aage wala 2 jawab ka hissa hai; usko chhorna ghalat hoga.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is part ko dobara (vii) likhti hai; yeh asal mein part (viii) hai. Answer key (page 297) \(\left(z-\frac{11-3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\frac{11+3i}{2}\right)\) likhti hai aur aage wala 2 chhor deti hai. Yeh product \(z^{2}-11z+\frac{65}{2}\) banta hai, jo diye gaye polynomial ka sirf aadha hai. Durust jawab: \(2z^{2}-22z+65=2\left(z-\frac{11-3i}{2}\right)\left(z-\frac{11+3i}{2}\right)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Factorize the following polynomial into its linear factors: \(z^{3}+8\)
blocks.explanation: Ab Sawal 2 mein humein polynomial ko linear factors (aise factors jin mein \(z\) ki power sirf 1 ho) mein torna hai. Yaad rakhiye: complex numbers mein degree 3 ke polynomial ke poore teen linear factors hote hain. \(z^{3}+8=z^{3}+2^{3}\) sum of cubes hai. Is se pehle ek linear factor aur ek quadratic milega; phir us quadratic ko completing the square aur \(i\) ki madad se do linear factors mein torenge.
steps:
Step 1: Sum of cubes lagayein
\[z^{3}+8=z^{3}+2^{3}\]
\[=(z+2)(z^{2}-2z+4)\]
Kyun: Sum of cubes ka formula hai \(A^{3}+B^{3}=(A+B)(A^{2}-AB+B^{2})\). Yahan \(A=z\), \(B=2\), kyun ke \(2^{3}=8\). Is se ek linear factor \((z+2)\) foran mil gaya.
Dhyan dein: Quadratic factor mein beech ka sign minus hai (\(-AB\)); students aksar yahan plus likh dete hain.

Step 2: Quadratic mein completing the square
\[z^{2}-2z+4=(z^{2}-2z+1)+3\]
\[=(z-1)^{2}+3\]
Kyun: \(-2\) ka aadha \(-1\) aur \((-1)^{2}=1\); is liye 4 ko \(1+3\) likha. Is quadratic ka discriminant \(4-16\) negative hai, yaani real factors nahi bante; isi liye \(i\) ki zaroorat hai.

Step 3: +3 ko minus square likh kar factorize karein
\[(i\sqrt{3})^{2}=3i^{2}=-3\]
\[(z-1)^{2}-(i\sqrt{3})^{2}\]
\[=(z-1-i\sqrt{3})(z-1+i\sqrt{3})\]
\[=\left(z-(1+i\sqrt{3})\right)\left(z-(1-i\sqrt{3})\right)\]
Kyun: 3 perfect square nahi, is liye \(\sqrt{3}\) liya: \((i\sqrt{3})^{2}=-3\). Phir \(A=z-1\), \(B=i\sqrt{3}\) le kar \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya. Aakhri line mein har factor ko \((z-\text{root})\) ki shakal mein likha taa ke roots saaf nazar aayein.

Tasdeeq: ek complex root check karein
\[(1+i\sqrt{3})^{2}=-2+2i\sqrt{3}\]
\[(1+i\sqrt{3})^{3}=(-2+2i\sqrt{3})(1+i\sqrt{3})\]
\[=-2-6=-8\]
Kyun: \(1+i\sqrt{3}\) ka cube \(-8\) aaya, yaani \(z=1+i\sqrt{3}\) rakhne se \(z^{3}+8=0\). Is ka matlab factor \(\left(z-(1+i\sqrt{3})\right)\) waqai durust hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{3}+8=(z+2)\left(z-(1-i\sqrt{3})\right)\left(z-(1+i\sqrt{3})\right)\). Teen linear factors: ek real root \(-2\) aur ek conjugate pair \(1\pm i\sqrt{3}\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Factorize the following polynomial into its linear factors: \(z^{3}+27\)
blocks.explanation: Tareeqa bilkul (i) wala hai, sirf ab \(27=3^{3}\) hai. Pehle sum of cubes se ek linear factor aur ek quadratic nikaalenge, phir quadratic ko completing the square se torenge. Yahan fractions aur \(\sqrt{3}\) dono aayenge, is liye har line aaram se likhiye.
steps:
Step 2: Completing the square
\[\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{9}{4}\]
\[9=\dfrac{9}{4}+\dfrac{27}{4}\]
\[z^{2}-3z+9=\left(z-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}+\dfrac{27}{4}\]
Kyun: \(-3\) ka aadha \(-\frac{3}{2}\) aur uska square \(\frac{9}{4}\). Constant 9 mein se \(\frac{9}{4}\) square poora karne mein lag gaya; baqi \(9-\frac{9}{4}=\frac{36-9}{4}=\frac{27}{4}\) bacha.

Step 3: Baqi ko minus square likhein
\[\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{27i^{2}}{4}=-\dfrac{27}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{27}{4}\) ka square root chahiye: \(\sqrt{27}=\sqrt{9\times3}=3\sqrt{3}\) aur \(\sqrt{4}=2\). Is liye \((3\sqrt{3})^{2}=27\), aur \(i\) lagane se \(+\frac{27}{4}=-\left(\frac{3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2}\).

Step 4: Difference of squares lagayein
\[\left(z-\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\]
\[\times\left(z-\dfrac{3}{2}+\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\]
\[=\left(z-\dfrac{3+3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\left(z-\dfrac{3-3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: \(A=z-\frac{3}{2}\), \(B=\frac{3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\) le kar \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) lagaya, phir har factor ko ek fraction mein jor kar \((z-\text{root})\) ki shakal di.
Dhyan dein: Minus bracket ke andar dono hisson par lagta hai: \(z-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{3\sqrt{3}i}{2}=z-\frac{3+3\sqrt{3}i}{2}\).

Tasdeeq: dono complex roots ka sum aur product
\[\dfrac{3+3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}+\dfrac{3-3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}=3\]
\[\dfrac{9+27}{4}=9\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}-3z+9\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a=3\) aur product \(c/a=9\) hona chahiye. Conjugates ka product (real part)\(^{2}\) + (imaginary part)\(^{2}\) hota hai: \(\frac{9}{4}+\frac{27}{4}=9\). Dono baatein poori hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{3}+27=(z+3)\left(z-\frac{3-3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\left(z-\frac{3+3\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)\). Ek real root \(-3\) aur ek conjugate pair.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) [printed as (ii)] Factorize the following polynomial into its linear factors: \(z^{3}-2z^{2}+16z-32\)
blocks.explanation: Yahan char terms hain aur koi seedha formula nazar nahi aata. Aise mein grouping try kijiye: pehli do terms ek group, aakhri do terms doosra group. Agar dono groups se ek hi bracket nikle to woh common factor ban jaata hai. Baqi jo squares ka sum bachega usko \(i\) se torenge. Kul teen linear factors milne chahiye, kyun ke degree 3 hai.
steps:
Step 1: Pairs mein group karein
\[z^{2}(z-2)+16(z-2)\]
\[=(z-2)(z^{2}+16)\]
Kyun: Pehle pair \(z^{3}-2z^{2}\) mein \(z^{2}\) common hai, doosre pair \(16z-32\) mein 16 common hai. Dono se same bracket \((z-2)\) bachta hai, jo ab poore expression ka common factor ban gaya.
Dhyan dein: Grouping tab hi kaam karti hai jab dono brackets bilkul ek jaise hon; agar na hon to terms ki tarteeb badal kar dekhiye.

Step 2: Squares ke sum ko torein
\[z^{2}+16=z^{2}-(4i)^{2}\]
\[=(z-4i)(z+4i)\]
Kyun: \((4i)^{2}=16i^{2}=-16\) hai, is liye \(+16=-(4i)^{2}\). Ab difference of squares hai aur \(A^{2}-B^{2}=(A+B)(A-B)\) seedha laga.

Tasdeeq: z = 4i rakhein
\[(4i)^{3}-2(4i)^{2}+16(4i)-32\]
\[=-64i+32+64i-32=0\]
Kyun: \((4i)^{3}=64i^{3}=-64i\) aur \((4i)^{2}=-16\). Sab jama karne par 0 aaya, yaani \(4i\) waqai root hai aur \((z-4i)\) factor hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{3}-2z^{2}+16z-32=(z-2)(z-4i)(z+4i)\). Ek real root 2 aur do imaginary roots \(\pm4i\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) [printed as (iii)] Factorize the following polynomial into its linear factors: \(z^{4}+21z^{2}-100\)
blocks.explanation: Is polynomial ko ghaur se dekhiye: is mein sirf \(z^{4}\), \(z^{2}\) aur constant hain, \(z^{3}\) ya \(z\) nahi. Is ka matlab yeh dar asal \(z^{2}\) mein quadratic hai. \(u=z^{2}\) rakhne se yeh aam quadratic ban jaata hai jo aap pehle se factorize karna jaante hain. Phir \(u\) ki jagah \(z^{2}\) wapas rakh kar har bracket ko linear factors mein torenge; degree 4 hai to kul char factors honge.
steps:
Step 1: Isko z² mein quadratic samjhein
\[u=z^{2}:\ u^{2}+21u-100\]
\[=(u+25)(u-4)\]
Kyun: Aise do numbers chahiye jinka product \(-100\) aur sum \(+21\) ho. Product negative hai to ek number positive aur ek negative hoga; \(25\) aur \(-4\) dono shartein poori karte hain.

Step 2: Wapas z mein likhein
\[z^{4}+21z^{2}-100=(z^{2}+25)(z^{2}-4)\]
Kyun: \(u\) sirf madad ke liye tha; ab \(u\) ki jagah \(z^{2}\) wapas rakha. Jawab hamesha asal variable \(z\) mein dena hai.

Step 3: Har bracket ko torein
\[z^{2}+25=z^{2}-(5i)^{2}\]
\[=(z+5i)(z-5i)\]
\[z^{2}-4=(z+2)(z-2)\]
Kyun: \(+25=-(5i)^{2}\) hai, to pehla bracket \(i\) ki madad se toota. \(z^{2}-4\) to seedha difference of squares hai, is ke liye \(i\) ki zaroorat nahi.
Dhyan dein: Sirf \((z^{2}+25)(z^{2}-4)\) par ruk jaana adhoora jawab hai; sawal linear factors maangta hai.

Tasdeeq: constant aur beech wali term
\[25\times(-4)=-100\]
\[25+(-4)=21\]
Kyun: Yeh dono numbers \(-100\) aur \(21z^{2}\) se milte hain, is liye pehla factorization sahih tha, aur baqi to sirf difference of squares tha.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) [printed as (iv)] Factorize the following polynomial into its linear factors: \(z^{4}-16\)
blocks.explanation: \(z^{4}-16\) ko pehchaniye: \(z^{4}=(z^{2})^{2}\) aur \(16=4^{2}\), yaani yeh difference of squares hai. Ek dafa formula lagane se do quadratic brackets milenge; phir har bracket ko dobara torenge, ek ko seedha aur doosre ko \(i\) ki madad se. Degree 4 hai, is liye char linear factors aane chahiye.
steps:
Step 2: Har bracket ko torein
\[z^{2}-4=(z-2)(z+2)\]
\[z^{2}+4=z^{2}-(2i)^{2}\]
\[=(z-2i)(z+2i)\]
Kyun: Pehla bracket phir se difference of squares hai. Doosre mein \((2i)^{2}=-4\) hai, is liye \(+4=-(2i)^{2}\) likh kar woh bhi difference of squares ban gaya.
Dhyan dein: Real numbers mein \(z^{2}+4\) par ruk jaate the; complex numbers mein yeh bhi toot-ta hai.

Tasdeeq: z = 2i rakhein
\[(2i)^{4}=16i^{4}=16\]
\[16-16=0\]
Kyun: \(i^{4}=1\) hai, is liye \((2i)^{4}=16\) aur \(z^{4}-16=0\). Yaani \(2i\) root hai, jaisa factor \((z-2i)\) bata raha hai.

steps:

\[z^{4}+3z^{2}-4=(z^{2}+4)(z^{2}-1)\]
Kyun: \(u=z^{2}\) samjhein to \(u^{2}+3u-4\) banta hai. Product \(-4\) aur sum 3 wale do numbers \(4\) aur \(-1\) hain, is liye \((u+4)(u-1)\), yaani \((z^{2}+4)(z^{2}-1)\).

Step 2: Har bracket ko torein
\[z^{2}+4=(z+2i)(z-2i)\]
\[z^{2}-1=(z+1)(z-1)\]
Kyun: \(+4=-(2i)^{2}\) likh kar pehla bracket difference of squares bana; \(z^{2}-1\) to seedha difference of squares hai.

Tasdeeq: constant aur beech wali term
\[4\times(-1)=-4\]
\[4+(-1)=3\]
Kyun: Yeh \(-4\) aur \(3z^{2}\) se milte hain, is liye pehla qadam sahih tha.

steps:
Step 1: z² mein quadratic ki tarah factorize karein
\[z^{4}+5z^{2}+6=(z^{2}+2)(z^{2}+3)\]
Kyun: \(u^{2}+5u+6\) mein product 6 aur sum 5 wale numbers 2 aur 3 hain. Dono positive hain, is liye dono brackets plus wale bane.

Step 2: Har plus ko minus square likhein
\[(\sqrt{2}\,i)^{2}=-2,\ (\sqrt{3}\,i)^{2}=-3\]
\[z^{2}+2=(z+\sqrt{2}\,i)(z-\sqrt{2}\,i)\]
\[z^{2}+3=(z+\sqrt{3}\,i)(z-\sqrt{3}\,i)\]
Kyun: 2 aur 3 perfect squares nahi, is liye unke square roots \(\sqrt{2}\) aur \(\sqrt{3}\) likhne padte hain; minus sign \(i\) se aata hai. Phir har bracket par difference of squares.
Dhyan dein: \((\sqrt{2}\,i)^{2}=2i^{2}=-2\), na ke \(-4\). \(\sqrt{2}\) ka square 2 hai.

Tasdeeq: constant aur beech wali term
\[2\times3=6\]
\[2+3=5\]
Kyun: Yeh \(+6\) aur \(5z^{2}\) se milte hain, is liye factorization durust hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z^{4}+5z^{2}+6=(z+\sqrt{2}\,i)(z-\sqrt{2}\,i)(z+\sqrt{3}\,i)(z-\sqrt{3}\,i)\). Chaaron roots imaginary hain: \(\pm\sqrt{2}\,i\) aur \(\pm\sqrt{3}\,i\).

steps:
Step 1: z² mein quadratic ki tarah factorize karein
\[z^{4}+7z^{2}-144=(z^{2}+16)(z^{2}-9)\]
Kyun: \(u^{2}+7u-144\) mein product \(-144\) aur sum 7 wale numbers 16 aur \(-9\) hain: \(16\times(-9)=-144\), \(16-9=7\). Bare numbers ke liye 144 ke factor pairs (\(12\times12\), \(16\times9\), ...) aik aik kar ke try kijiye.

Step 2: Har bracket ko torein
\[z^{2}+16=(z+4i)(z-4i)\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is sawal ke aath parts ke labels (i), (ii), (ii), (iii), (iv), (iii), (iv), (v) chhapti hai; yahan unko (i) se (viii) tak number kiya gaya hai. blocks.prompt: 3 Find the roots of \(z^{4}+7z^{2}-144=0\) and hence express it as a product of linear factors.
blocks.explanation: Is sawal ke do hisse hain: pehle equation ke roots nikaalne hain, phir unhi roots ki madad se polynomial ko linear factors ke product mein likhna hai. Degree 4 hai, is liye char roots aayenge. Equation mein sirf \(z^{4}\), \(z^{2}\) aur constant hain, is liye \(u=z^{2}\) rakh kar isko \(u\) mein aam quadratic banayenge, \(u\) nikaalenge, phir square root lenge. Aakhir mein Fundamental Theorem of Algebra ke corollary (natije) ke mutabiq har root \(r\) se ek linear factor \((z-r)\) banta hai.
steps:
Step 1: u mein quadratic banayein
\[u=z^{2}\]
\[u^{2}+7u-144=0\]
Kyun: \(z^{4}=(z^{2})^{2}=u^{2}\). Is tarah degree 4 ki equation ek aam quadratic ban jaati hai, jise hum pehle se solve karna jaante hain. Naya variable rakhna sirf kaam aasaan karne ki chaal hai.

Step 2: u nikaalein
\[u=\dfrac{-7\pm\sqrt{49+576}}{2}\]
\[=\dfrac{-7\pm25}{2}\]
\[u=9\ \text{or}\ u=-16\]
Kyun: Quadratic formula mein \(a=1\), \(b=7\), \(c=-144\) rakha: \(b^{2}-4ac=49+576=625\) aur \(\sqrt{625}=25\). Plus wale sign se \(\frac{18}{2}=9\), minus wale se \(\frac{-32}{2}=-16\). (\((u-9)(u+16)\) factorize kar ke bhi yahi milta hai.)

Step 3: Wapas z par aayein
\[z^{2}=9\Rightarrow z=\pm3\]
\[z^{2}=-16\Rightarrow z=\pm\sqrt{-16}=\pm4i\]
Kyun: Hum ne \(u\) nikala tha, lekin sawal \(z\) maangta hai. Square root lene par hamesha do values aati hain, \(\pm\). Aur \(\sqrt{-16}=\sqrt{16}\,\sqrt{-1}=4i\).
Dhyan dein: \(u=-16\) dekh kar yeh mat sochiye ke "koi jawab nahi"; complex numbers mein iske do roots \(\pm4i\) hain. \(\pm\) bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai.

Step 4: Linear factors likhein
\[z^{4}+7z^{2}-144\]
\[=(z-3)(z+3)(z-4i)(z+4i)\]
Kyun: \(z^{4}\) ka coefficient 1 hai, is liye \(P(z)=1\cdot(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})(z-z_{3})(z-z_{4})\). Root \(-3\) se \((z-(-3))=(z+3)\) banta hai; sign ka khayal rakhiye.

Tasdeeq: z = 4i rakhein
\[(4i)^{4}+7(4i)^{2}-144\]
\[=256-112-144=0\]
Kyun: \(4i\) equation ko satisfy karta hai; \(\pm3\) bhi karte hain (\(81+63-144=0\)). Yeh wahi jawab hai jo Sawal 2 ke aakhri part mein aaya tha, sirf raasta mukhtalif hai.
blocks.final_answer: Roots: \(3,\ -3,\ 4i,\ -4i\); \(z^{4}+7z^{2}-144=(z+3)(z-3)(z+4i)(z-4i)\). Char roots, char linear factors: har root ka apna ek factor.

blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Solve the following complex quadratic equation by completing square method: \(2z^{2}-3z+4=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh "completing the square" wala sawal hai, is liye quadratic formula seedha nahi lagana, balke us ka tareeqa qadam ba qadam dikhana hai. Tarteeb yaad kar lijiye: (1) \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banayein, (2) constant ko right side le jaayein, (3) dono taraf (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) jorein taa ke left side perfect square ban jaaye, (4) square root lein. Right side negative aayegi, is liye roots complex honge aur \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\) kaam aayega.
steps:
Step 1: 2 se divide karein aur constant ko right par le jaayein
\[z^{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}z+2=0\]
\[z^{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}z=-2\]
Kyun: Completing the square ke liye \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 hona zaroori hai. Equation ke dono taraf ko 2 se divide karna jaaiz hai, kyun ke \(0\div2=0\) hi rehta hai. Phir 2 ko right side le gaye taa ke left side par square banane ki jagah ho.

Step 2: Dono taraf (3/4)² jorein
\[\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{9}{16}\]
\[\left(z-\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{2}=-2+\dfrac{9}{16}\]
\[=-\dfrac{23}{16}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{3}{2}\) ka aadha \(\frac{3}{4}\) hai aur uska square \(\frac{9}{16}\). Dono taraf ek hi number jorne se equation barabar rehti hai, aur left side perfect square \(\left(z-\frac{3}{4}\right)^{2}\) ban jaati hai. Right side: \(-\frac{32}{16}+\frac{9}{16}=-\frac{23}{16}\).
Dhyan dein: Sirf left side par jorna aur right side bhool jaana bohat aam ghalti hai.

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z-\dfrac{3}{4}=\pm\sqrt{-\dfrac{23}{16}}=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{23}}{4}\,i\]
\[z=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{23}\,i}{4}\]
Kyun: Jab \(k>0\) ho to \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\); yahan \(\sqrt{16}=4\) neeche aa gaya. Phir dono taraf \(\frac{3}{4}\) jora. \(\pm\) zaroor likhiye, warna ek root kho jaayega.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=\dfrac{6}{4}=\dfrac{3}{2}=-\dfrac{b}{a}\]
\[\text{product}=\dfrac{9+23}{16}=2=\dfrac{c}{a}\]
Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain. Yahan \(-b/a=3/2\) aur \(c/a=4/2=2\), dono mil gaye.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=\frac{3\pm i\sqrt{23}}{4}\). Do complex roots jo aapas mein conjugate hain.

\[z^{2}-6z=-30\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient pehle se 1 hai, is liye divide karne ki zaroorat nahi. 30 ko right side le gaye.

Step 2: Dono taraf 3² = 9 jorein
\[z^{2}-6z+9=-30+9\]
\[(z-3)^{2}=-21\]
Kyun: \(-6\) ka aadha \(-3\) aur \((-3)^{2}=9\). Dono taraf 9 jorne se left side \((z-3)^{2}\) ban gayi.

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z-3=\pm\sqrt{-21}=\pm i\sqrt{21}\]
\[z=3\pm i\sqrt{21}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{-21}=i\sqrt{21}\); 21 perfect square nahi, is liye \(\sqrt{21}\) wese hi rehta hai. Phir dono taraf 3 jora.
Dhyan dein: Real part 3 hai, jo \(-6\) ke aadhe se aaya. Answer key yahan 2 likhti hai; neeche correction dekhiye.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=6=-\dfrac{b}{a}\]

Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Solve the following complex quadratic equation by completing square method: \(3z^{2}-18z+50=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh "completing the square" wala sawal hai, is liye quadratic formula seedha nahi lagana, balke us ka tareeqa qadam ba qadam dikhana hai. Tarteeb yaad kar lijiye: (1) \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banayein, (2) constant ko right side le jaayein, (3) dono taraf (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) jorein taa ke left side perfect square ban jaaye, (4) square root lein. Right side negative aayegi, is liye roots complex honge aur \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\) kaam aayega.
steps:
Step 1: 3 se divide karein aur constant ko right par le jaayein
\[z^{2}-6z+\dfrac{50}{3}=0\]
\[z^{2}-6z=-\dfrac{50}{3}\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banana hai. \(18\div3=6\) saaf aata hai, lekin 50 ko 3 poora divide nahi karta, is liye \(\frac{50}{3}\) fraction hi rehta hai.

Step 2: Dono taraf 3² = 9 jorein
\[(z-3)^{2}=9-\dfrac{50}{3}\]
\[=\dfrac{27-50}{3}=-\dfrac{23}{3}\]
Kyun: \(-6\) ka aadha \(-3\) aur uska square 9. Right side par 9 ko \(\frac{27}{3}\) likha taa ke denominators ek jaise hon aur ghataana aasaan ho.

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z-3=\pm i\sqrt{\dfrac{23}{3}}\]
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{23}{3}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{69}}{3}\]
\[z=3\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{69}}{3}\,i\]
Kyun: Negative number ka square root \(i\) deta hai. Denominator mein root achha nahi lagta, is liye upar neeche \(\sqrt{3}\) se zarb diya: \(\frac{\sqrt{23}\sqrt{3}}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{69}}{3}\). Is ko rationalize karna (denominator se root hatana) kehte hain.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=6=\dfrac{18}{3}\]
\[\text{product}=9+\dfrac{69}{9}=\dfrac{50}{3}\]
Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain. Yahan \(-b/a=18/3=6\) aur \(c/a=50/3\); dono mil gaye. Answer key wala \(3\pm i\) is jaanch mein fail ho jaata hai (product 10 aata hai).
blocks.final_answer: \(z=3\pm\frac{\sqrt{69}}{3}\,i=\frac{9\pm i\sqrt{69}}{3}\). Dono shaklein barabar hain.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) [printed as (i)] Solve the following complex quadratic equation by completing square method: \(z^{2}+4z+13=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh "completing the square" wala sawal hai, is liye quadratic formula seedha nahi lagana, balke us ka tareeqa qadam ba qadam dikhana hai. Tarteeb yaad kar lijiye: (1) \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banayein, (2) constant ko right side le jaayein, (3) dono taraf (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) jorein taa ke left side perfect square ban jaaye, (4) square root lein. Right side negative aayegi, is liye roots complex honge aur \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\) kaam aayega.
steps:
Step 1: Constant ko right par le jaayein
\[z^{2}+4z=-13\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient pehle se 1 hai, is liye seedha 13 ko right side le gaye.

Step 2: Dono taraf 2² = 4 jorein
\[z^{2}+4z+4=-13+4\]
\[(z+2)^{2}=-9\]
Kyun: 4 ka aadha 2 aur \(2^{2}=4\). Dono taraf 4 jora; left side \((z+2)^{2}\) ban gayi aur right side \(-9\).

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z+2=\pm\sqrt{-9}=\pm3i\]
\[z=-2\pm3i\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{-9}=\sqrt{9}\,i=3i\). Phir dono taraf se 2 ghataya.
Dhyan dein: \(z+2\) se \(z\) nikaalte waqt 2 minus hota hai, is liye real part \(-2\) hai, \(+2\) nahi.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=-4=-\dfrac{b}{a}\]
\[\text{product}=4+9=13=\dfrac{c}{a}\]
Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=-2\pm3i\). Yeh wahi roots hain jo factors \((z+2-3i)(z+2+3i)\) dete hain.

blocks.prompt: 4 (v) [printed as (ii)] Solve the following complex quadratic equation by completing square method: \(2z^{2}+6z+9=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh "completing the square" wala sawal hai, is liye quadratic formula seedha nahi lagana, balke us ka tareeqa qadam ba qadam dikhana hai. Tarteeb yaad kar lijiye: (1) \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banayein, (2) constant ko right side le jaayein, (3) dono taraf (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) jorein taa ke left side perfect square ban jaaye, (4) square root lein. Right side negative aayegi, is liye roots complex honge aur \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\) kaam aayega.
steps:
Step 1: 2 se divide karein aur constant ko right par le jaayein
\[z^{2}+3z+\dfrac{9}{2}=0\]
\[z^{2}+3z=-\dfrac{9}{2}\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banana hai, is liye har term ko 2 se divide kiya.

Step 2: Dono taraf (3/2)² jorein
\[\left(z+\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}=-\dfrac{9}{2}+\dfrac{9}{4}\]
\[=-\dfrac{9}{4}\]
Kyun: 3 ka aadha \(\frac{3}{2}\) aur \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}=\frac{9}{4}\). Right side: \(-\frac{18}{4}+\frac{9}{4}=-\frac{9}{4}\).

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z+\dfrac{3}{2}=\pm\dfrac{3}{2}\,i\]
\[z=-\dfrac{3}{2}\pm\dfrac{3}{2}\,i\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{-\frac{9}{4}}=\frac{3}{2}i\), kyun ke \(\sqrt{9}=3\) aur \(\sqrt{4}=2\). Phir dono taraf se \(\frac{3}{2}\) ghataya. Dilchasp baat: yahan real aur imaginary parts ki size barabar hai.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=-3=-\dfrac{6}{2}\]
\[\text{product}=\dfrac{9}{4}+\dfrac{9}{4}=\dfrac{9}{2}\]
Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=-\frac{3}{2}\pm\frac{3}{2}i\). Doosre lafzon mein \(z=\frac{3}{2}(-1\pm i)\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (vi) [printed as (iii)] Solve the following complex quadratic equation by completing square method: \(3z^{2}-5z+7=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh "completing the square" wala sawal hai, is liye quadratic formula seedha nahi lagana, balke us ka tareeqa qadam ba qadam dikhana hai. Tarteeb yaad kar lijiye: (1) \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banayein, (2) constant ko right side le jaayein, (3) dono taraf (z ke coefficient ka aadha)\(^{2}\) jorein taa ke left side perfect square ban jaaye, (4) square root lein. Right side negative aayegi, is liye roots complex honge aur \(\sqrt{-k}=i\sqrt{k}\) kaam aayega.
steps:
Step 1: 3 se divide karein aur constant ko right par le jaayein
\[z^{2}-\dfrac{5}{3}z+\dfrac{7}{3}=0\]
\[z^{2}-\dfrac{5}{3}z=-\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 banana hai. Fractions aa gaye, lekin tareeqa wahi hai.

Step 2: Dono taraf (5/6)² jorein
\[\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{5}{3}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{25}{36}\]
\[\left(z-\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^{2}=-\dfrac{7}{3}+\dfrac{25}{36}\]
\[=\dfrac{-84+25}{36}=-\dfrac{59}{36}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{5}{3}\) ka aadha \(\frac{5}{6}\) hai, uska square \(\frac{25}{36}\). Jorne ke liye common denominator 36 liya: \(\frac{7}{3}=\frac{84}{36}\).
Dhyan dein: Yahin answer key ghalti karti hai; \(-84+25=-59\) hai, \(-41\) nahi. Fractions ko aaram se jama kijiye.

Step 3: Square root lein
\[z-\dfrac{5}{6}=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{59}}{6}\,i\]
\[z=\dfrac{5\pm i\sqrt{59}}{6}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{36}=6\), is liye \(\sqrt{-\frac{59}{36}}=\frac{\sqrt{59}}{6}i\). 59 prime number hai, is ka \(\sqrt{59}\) aur saada nahi hota. Phir dono taraf \(\frac{5}{6}\) jora.

Tasdeeq: sum aur product
\[\text{sum}=\dfrac{10}{6}=\dfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\text{product}=\dfrac{25+59}{36}=\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Kyun: \(az^{2}+bz+c=0\) ke roots ka sum \(-b/a\) aur product \(c/a\) hota hai. Yeh jaanch bohat tez hai: jawab ko wapas equation mein rakhne ki lambi mehnat ke baghair pata chal jaata hai ke roots sahih hain. Yahan \(-b/a=5/3\) aur \(c/a=7/3\); dono mil gaye (\(\frac{84}{36}=\frac{7}{3}\)).
blocks.final_answer: \(z=\frac{5\pm i\sqrt{59}}{6}\). Conjugate pair, real part \(\frac{5}{6}\).

blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Solve the following equations: \(2z^{4}-32=0\)
blocks.explanation: Sawal 5 mein equations solve karni hain, yaani \(z\) ki woh saari values nikaalni hain jin se equation sahih ho jaaye. Pehle degree dekhiye: yahan 4 hai, to char roots aayenge. Common factor 2 bahar nikaalenge, phir \(z^{4}-16\) ko poora factorize karenge (yeh Sawal 2 mein kar chuke hain), aur har factor ko zero ke barabar rakhenge.
steps:
Step 1: Common factor 2 bahar nikaalein
\[2(z^{4}-16)=0\]
\[z^{4}-16=0\]
Kyun: 2 kabhi zero nahi hota, is liye agar \(2\times(\ldots)=0\) hai to bracket hi zero hoga. Dono taraf 2 se divide karna bhi yahi baat hai.

Step 2: Poora factorize karein
\[(z^{2}-4)(z^{2}+4)=0\]
\[(z-2)(z+2)(z-2i)(z+2i)=0\]
Kyun: Pehle \(z^{4}-16=(z^{2})^{2}-4^{2}\) par difference of squares, phir \(z^{2}-4\) par dobara, aur \(z^{2}+4\) par \(+4=-(2i)^{2}\) likh kar teesri dafa.

Step 3: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[z=2,\ -2,\ 2i,\ -2i\]
Kyun: Product tabhi zero hota hai jab koi ek factor zero ho (zero product rule). Har factor se ek root mila.

Tasdeeq: z = 2i rakhein
\[2(2i)^{4}-32=2(16)-32=0\]
Kyun: \((2i)^{4}=16i^{4}=16\), kyun ke \(i^{4}=1\). Equation poori hui, to \(2i\) sahih root hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=\pm2,\ \pm2i\). Do real aur do imaginary roots.

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Solve the following equations: \(3z^{5}-243z=0\)
blocks.explanation: Degree 5 hai, to paanch roots aane chahiye. Dono terms mein \(3z\) common hai, usko bahar nikaalenge, phir \(z^{4}-81\) ko poora factorize karenge. Ek ahem baat: equation ko \(z\) se divide mat kijiye, warna root \(z=0\) kho jaayega. Common factor nikaalna mehfooz tareeqa hai.
steps:
Step 1: 3z bahar nikaalein
\[3z(z^{4}-81)=0\]
Kyun: \(3z^{5}=3z\cdot z^{4}\) aur \(243z=3z\cdot81\), kyun ke \(243\div3=81\).
Dhyan dein: \(z\) se divide karte to \(3z^{4}-243=0\) bachta aur \(z=0\) wala root ghayab ho jaata.

Step 2: z⁴ − 81 factorize karein
\[z^{4}-81=(z^{2}-9)(z^{2}+9)\]
\[=(z-3)(z+3)(z-3i)(z+3i)\]
Kyun: \(81=9^{2}\), is liye pehle difference of squares; phir \(z^{2}-9\) dobara, aur \(+9=-(3i)^{2}\) likh kar \(z^{2}+9\) bhi toda.

Step 3: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[3z(z-3)(z+3)(z-3i)(z+3i)=0\]
\[z=0,\ 3,\ -3,\ 3i,\ -3i\]
Kyun: \(3z=0\) se \(z=0\) aata hai, aur baqi char factors se baqi char roots. Kul paanch, jitni degree.

Tasdeeq: z = 3i rakhein
\[3(3i)^{5}-243(3i)\]
\[=3(243i)-729i=0\]
Kyun: \((3i)^{5}=243\,i^{5}=243i\), kyun ke \(i^{5}=i^{4}\cdot i=i\). Dono terms \(729i\) ban kar cancel ho gayin.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=0,\ \pm3,\ \pm3i\). Paanch roots, degree ke barabar.

blocks.prompt: 5 (iii) Solve the following equations: \(5z^{5}-5z=0\)
blocks.explanation: Yeh (ii) ka chhota bhai hai. Degree 5 hai, to paanch roots chahiye. Dono terms mein \(5z\) common hai; usko bahar nikaal kar \(z^{4}-1\) ko poora factorize karenge. Yahan bhi \(z\) se divide nahi karna, taa ke \(z=0\) wala root mehfooz rahe.
steps:
Step 1: 5z bahar nikaalein
\[5z(z^{4}-1)=0\]
Kyun: Dono terms mein 5 aur \(z\) common hain: \(5z^{5}=5z\cdot z^{4}\) aur \(5z=5z\cdot1\).

Step 2: z⁴ − 1 factorize karein
\[z^{4}-1=(z^{2}-1)(z^{2}+1)\]
\[=(z-1)(z+1)(z-i)(z+i)\]
Kyun: Pehle \((z^{2})^{2}-1^{2}\) par difference of squares, phir \(z^{2}-1\) par dobara, aur \(+1=-i^{2}\) likh kar \(z^{2}+1=(z-i)(z+i)\).

Step 3: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[z=0,\ 1,\ -1,\ i,\ -i\]
Kyun: Ek root \(5z\) se aata hai aur char roots char brackets se. Ghaur kijiye: \(1,-1,i,-i\) wahi "fourth roots of unity" hain jo aap aage Section 1.5 mein parhenge.

Tasdeeq: z = i rakhein
\[5i^{5}-5i=5i-5i=0\]
Kyun: \(i^{5}=i^{4}\cdot i=i\), is liye dono terms barabar ho kar cancel ho gayin.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=0,\ \pm1,\ \pm i\). Paanch roots.

blocks.prompt: 5 (iv) Solve the following equations: \(z^{3}-5z^{2}+z-5=0\)
blocks.explanation: Char terms wali cubic equation hai aur koi formula seedha nahi lagta. Aise mein grouping try kijiye: pehli do terms aur aakhri do terms alag alag group. Agar dono se ek hi bracket nikle to woh common factor ban jaata hai, aur jo squares ka sum bachega usko \(i\) se torenge. Degree 3 hai, to teen roots.
steps:
Step 1: Pairs mein group karein
\[z^{2}(z-5)+1(z-5)=0\]
\[(z-5)(z^{2}+1)=0\]
Kyun: Pehle pair \(z^{3}-5z^{2}\) se \(z^{2}\) nikla aur \((z-5)\) bacha; doosre pair \(z-5\) se 1 nikla aur wahi \((z-5)\) bacha. Is liye \((z-5)\) common le liya.

Step 2: z² + 1 factorize karein
\[(z-5)(z-i)(z+i)=0\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}+1=z^{2}-i^{2}\), kyun ke \(-i^{2}=+1\). Phir difference of squares.

Step 3: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[z=5,\ i,\ -i\]
Kyun: Teen factors, teen roots. Ek real aur ek conjugate pair.

Tasdeeq: z = 5 rakhein
\[125-125+5-5=0\]
Kyun: \(5^{3}=125\), \(5\cdot5^{2}=125\); sab cancel ho kar 0 aaya, to \(z=5\) equation ko satisfy karta hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=5,\ \pm i\). Ek real root aur do imaginary roots.

blocks.prompt: 5 (v) Solve the following equations: \(4z^{4}-25z^{2}+21=0\)
blocks.explanation: Is equation mein sirf \(z^{4}\), \(z^{2}\) aur constant hain, yaani yeh \(z^{2}\) mein quadratic hai. \(u=z^{2}\) rakh kar \(u\) nikaalenge, phir square root le kar \(z\). Yahan ek mazay ki baat hai: chaaron roots real aate hain. Har sawal mein \(i\) aana zaroori nahi; jo hisaab kahe wahi jawab hai.
steps:
Step 1: u = z² rakhein
\[4u^{2}-25u+21=0\]
Kyun: \(z^{4}=(z^{2})^{2}=u^{2}\). Ab yeh aam quadratic hai.

Step 2: Middle term tor kar factorize karein
\[4u^{2}-21u-4u+21=0\]
\[u(4u-21)-1(4u-21)=0\]
\[(4u-21)(u-1)=0\]
Kyun: \(a\times c=4\times21=84\). Aise do numbers chahiye jinka product 84 aur sum \(-25\) ho: woh \(-21\) aur \(-4\) hain. Middle term ko in do mein tor kar grouping ki.

Step 3: Pehle u, phir z nikaalein
\[u=\dfrac{21}{4}\Rightarrow z=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\]
\[u=1\Rightarrow z=\pm1\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}=u\) ka square root lene par do values aati hain. \(\sqrt{\frac{21}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{21}}{\sqrt{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: Dono \(u\) positive hain, is liye yahan \(i\) nahi aata; sirf \(\pm\) yaad rakhiye.

Tasdeeq: z = 1 rakhein
\[4-25+21=0\]
Kyun: \(z=1\) equation ko satisfy karta hai. (\(z^{2}=\frac{21}{4}\) rakhein to \(4\cdot\frac{441}{16}-25\cdot\frac{21}{4}+21=0\) bhi aata hai.)
blocks.final_answer: \(z=\pm1,\ \pm\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\). Chaaron roots real hain.

blocks.prompt: 5 (vi) Solve the following equations: \(z^{3}+z^{2}+z+1=0\)
blocks.explanation: Char terms hain, is liye grouping ka tareeqa: pehli do terms aur aakhri do terms. Common bracket nikalega, phir \(z^{2}+1\) ko \(i\) se torenge. Degree 3 hai, to teen roots.
steps:
Step 1: Pairs mein group karein
\[z^{2}(z+1)+1(z+1)=0\]
\[(z+1)(z^{2}+1)=0\]
Kyun: \(z^{3}+z^{2}\) se \(z^{2}\) nikla aur \(z+1\) se 1; dono pairs mein \((z+1)\) hai, woh common le liya.

Step 2: z² + 1 factorize karein
\[(z+1)(z-i)(z+i)=0\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}+1=z^{2}-i^{2}\), phir difference of squares.

Step 3: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[z=-1,\ i,\ -i\]
Kyun: Har factor se ek root mila: \(z+1=0\) se \(-1\), \(z-i=0\) se \(i\), \(z+i=0\) se \(-i\).
Dhyan dein: \(z+1=0\) ka root \(-1\) hai, \(+1\) nahi.

Tasdeeq: z = i rakhein
\[i^{3}+i^{2}+i+1\]
\[=-i-1+i+1=0\]
Kyun: \(i^{3}=-i\) aur \(i^{2}=-1\). Sab cancel ho gaya, to \(i\) sahih root hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z=-1,\ \pm i\). Ek real root aur ek conjugate pair.

blocks.prompt: 6 Find a polynomial of degree 3 with zeros \(3,\ -2i,\ 2i\) and satisfying \(P(1)=20\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh ulta sawal hai: pehle hum polynomial se roots nikaalte the, ab roots (zeros) diye gaye hain aur polynomial banana hai. Qaida: har zero \(r\) se ek factor \((z-r)\) banta hai, aur \(P(z)=a(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})\cdots\), jahan aage ek na-maloom number \(a\) hai. Yeh \(a\) is liye zaroori hai ke same zeros wale bohat se polynomials ho sakte hain (sirf aage ka number mukhtalif); di gayi shart (condition) \(a\) ko tay kar deti hai. Phir expand kar ke jawab ki tasdeeq karenge.
steps:
Step 1: Factors likhein
\[P(z)=a(z-3)(z+2i)(z-2i)\]
Kyun: Zero 3 se \((z-3)\), zero \(-2i\) se \((z-(-2i))=(z+2i)\), aur zero \(2i\) se \((z-2i)\). Degree 3 hai, is liye teen factors.
Dhyan dein: Negative zero ka factor plus wala banta hai; \(-2i\) se \((z-2i)\) likhna aam ghalti hai.

Step 2: Conjugate pair ko multiply karein
\[(z+2i)(z-2i)=z^{2}-4i^{2}=z^{2}+4\]
\[P(z)=a(z-3)(z^{2}+4)\]
Kyun: Conjugate pair (jora) ka product hamesha real quadratic hota hai, kyun ke \(-4i^{2}=+4\) ban jaata hai aur \(i\) khatam. Is liye pehle yeh pair zarb dena kaam ko saaf kar deta hai.

Step 3: P(1) = 20 se a nikaalein
\[P(1)=a(1-3)(1+4)=-10a\]
\[-10a=20\Rightarrow a=-2\]
Kyun: \(P(1)\) ka matlab hai har jagah \(z=1\) rakhna. \((1-3)=-2\) aur \((1+4)=5\), product \(-10a\). Isko 20 ke barabar rakh kar \(a=-2\) mila.

Step 4: Expand karein
\[(z-3)(z^{2}+4)=z^{3}-3z^{2}+4z-12\]
\[P(z)=-2z^{3}+6z^{2}-8z+24\]
Kyun: Pehle bracket ki har term ko doosre ki har term se zarb diya, phir poore natije ko \(-2\) se. Negative number se zarb dene par har sign ulta ho jaata hai.

Tasdeeq: P(1) aur P(3)
\[P(1)=-2+6-8+24=20\]
\[P(3)=-54+54-24+24=0\]
Kyun: Shart \(P(1)=20\) poori hai, aur \(P(3)=0\) se pata chalta hai ke 3 waqai zero hai. Dono baatein mil gayin, is liye polynomial sahih hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 Find a polynomial of degree 4 with zeros \(2i,\ -2i,\ 1,\ -1\), and satisfying \(P(2)=240\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh ulta sawal hai: pehle hum polynomial se roots nikaalte the, ab roots (zeros) diye gaye hain aur polynomial banana hai. Qaida: har zero \(r\) se ek factor \((z-r)\) banta hai, aur \(P(z)=a(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})\cdots\), jahan aage ek na-maloom number \(a\) hai. Yeh \(a\) is liye zaroori hai ke same zeros wale bohat se polynomials ho sakte hain (sirf aage ka number mukhtalif); di gayi shart (condition) \(a\) ko tay kar deti hai. Phir expand kar ke jawab ki tasdeeq karenge. Yahan zeros do pairs mein aate hain: \(\pm2i\) aur \(\pm1\).
steps:
Step 1: Factors likh kar pairs banayein
\[P(z)=a(z-2i)(z+2i)(z-1)(z+1)\]
\[=a(z^{2}+4)(z^{2}-1)\]
Kyun: Har pair difference of squares hai: \((z-2i)(z+2i)=z^{2}-4i^{2}=z^{2}+4\) aur \((z-1)(z+1)=z^{2}-1\). Pairs mein zarb dena hisaab ko bohat chhota kar deta hai.

Step 2: P(2) = 240 se a nikaalein
\[P(2)=a(4+4)(4-1)=24a\]
\[24a=240\Rightarrow a=10\]
Kyun: \(z=2\) rakhne par \(z^{2}=4\). Is liye \((4+4)=8\) aur \((4-1)=3\), product \(24a\). Isko 240 ke barabar rakha.

Step 3: Expand karein
\[(z^{2}+4)(z^{2}-1)=z^{4}+3z^{2}-4\]
\[P(z)=10z^{4}+30z^{2}-40\]
Kyun: \(z^{4}-z^{2}+4z^{2}-4\) mein \(-z^{2}+4z^{2}=3z^{2}\). Phir har term ko 10 se zarb diya.
Dhyan dein: \(z^{3}\) aur \(z\) wali terms nahi aatin, kyun ke zeros \(\pm\) pairs mein hain; is mein koi ghalti nahi.

blocks.prompt: 8 Find a polynomial of degree 4 with zeros \(4,\ -4,\ 1+i,\ 1-i\) and satisfying \(P(2)=72\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh ulta sawal hai: pehle hum polynomial se roots nikaalte the, ab roots (zeros) diye gaye hain aur polynomial banana hai. Qaida: har zero \(r\) se ek factor \((z-r)\) banta hai, aur \(P(z)=a(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})\cdots\), jahan aage ek na-maloom number \(a\) hai. Yeh \(a\) is liye zaroori hai ke same zeros wale bohat se polynomials ho sakte hain (sirf aage ka number mukhtalif); di gayi shart (condition) \(a\) ko tay kar deti hai. Phir expand kar ke jawab ki tasdeeq karenge. Yahan \(1+i\) aur \(1-i\) ek conjugate pair hain, aur \(4\), \(-4\) ek real pair.
steps:
Step 1: Real pair multiply karein
\[(z-4)(z+4)=z^{2}-16\]
Kyun: Zeros 4 aur \(-4\) se factors \((z-4)\) aur \((z+4)\) bante hain; in ka product seedha difference of squares hai.

Step 2: Conjugate pair multiply karein
\[(z-1-i)(z-1+i)=(z-1)^{2}-i^{2}\]
\[=z^{2}-2z+1+1\]
\[=z^{2}-2z+2\]
Kyun: Zero \(1+i\) ka factor \(z-(1+i)=z-1-i\) hai. \((z-1)\) ko ek block \(A\) samjhiye: \((A-i)(A+i)=A^{2}-i^{2}=A^{2}+1\). Natija real quadratic hai, \(i\) khatam.
Dhyan dein: \(z-(1+i)\) mein minus dono hisson par lagta hai: \(z-1-i\), na ke \(z-1+i\).

Step 3: P(2) = 72 se a nikaalein
\[P(z)=a(z^{2}-16)(z^{2}-2z+2)\]
\[P(2)=a(-12)(2)=-24a\]
\[-24a=72\Rightarrow a=-3\]
Kyun: \(z=2\) rakha: \(4-16=-12\) aur \(4-4+2=2\). Product \(-24a\) ko 72 ke barabar rakh kar \(a=-3\).

Step 4: Expand karein
\[(z^{2}-16)(z^{2}-2z+2)\]
\[=z^{4}-2z^{3}-14z^{2}+32z-32\]
\[P(z)=-3z^{4}+6z^{3}+42z^{2}-96z+96\]
Kyun: \(z^{2}\) ko teeno terms se, phir \(-16\) ko teeno terms se zarb diya; milti julti terms jama ki: \(2z^{2}-16z^{2}=-14z^{2}\). Aakhir mein \(-3\) se zarb diya, har sign ulta ho gaya.

Tasdeeq: P(2)
\[-48+48+168-192+96=72\]
Kyun: \(z=2\) rakhne par 72 aaya, shart poori ho gayi. Is se expansion aur \(a\) dono ki tasdeeq ho gayi.
